title: Retail Salespersons
description: Sell merchandise, such as furniture, motor vehicles, appliances, or apparel to consumers.

tasks.text: Compute sales prices, total purchases, and receive and process cash or credit payment.
Estimate and quote trade-in allowances.
Estimate quantity and cost of merchandise required, such as paint or floor covering.
Estimate cost of repair or alteration of merchandise.
Prepare merchandise for purchase or rental.
Ticket, arrange, and display merchandise to promote sales.
Bag or package purchases and wrap gifts.
Maintain records related to sales.
Prepare sales slips or sales contracts.
Place special orders or call other stores to find desired items.
Demonstrate use or operation of merchandise.
Sell or arrange for delivery, insurance, financing, or service contracts for merchandise.
Help customers try on or fit merchandise.
Rent merchandise to customers.
Greet customers and ascertain what each customer wants or needs.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Recommend, select, and help locate or obtain merchandise based on customer needs and desires.
Answer questions regarding the store and its merchandise.
Maintain knowledge of current sales and promotions, policies regarding payment and exchanges, and security practices.
Open and close cash registers, performing tasks such as counting money, separating charge slips, coupons, and vouchers, balancing cash drawers, and making deposits.
Describe merchandise and explain use, operation, and care of merchandise to customers.
Inventory stock and requisition new stock.
Exchange merchandise for customers and accept returns.
Watch for and recognize security risks and thefts and know how to prevent or handle these situations.
Clean shelves, counters, and tables.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, SmugMug Flickr.

skills.name: Internet browser software
skills.def: Software to view the contents of web pages and to navigate from one page to another. Examples: Apple Safari, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple macOS, Handheld computer device software, Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat, Microsoft SharePoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Google Docs, Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Enterprise resource planning ERP software
skills.def: Software to integrate, monitor, or analyze data from multiple business operations within a unified system. Examples: Oracle PeopleSoft, SAP software.
